definitions.explanation: Having the same form, manner, or degree throughout. Describes a situation where there is no variation among multiple elements.

examples.japanese: {一様|いちよう}に{並|なら}んでいる。
{参加者|さんかしゃ}は{一様|いちよう}に{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: The participants were all equally surprised.

examples.japanese: {結果|けっか}は{一様|いちよう}ではなく、{地域|ちいき}によって{差|さ}があった。
examples.english: The results were not uniform; there were differences by region.

notes:
{一様|いちよう} describes uniformity or sameness across multiple items or people. It is commonly used as an adverb ({一様|いちよう}に) or as a na-adjective ({一様|いちよう}な).

WORD FORMATION:
{一|いち} (one) + {様|よう} (manner, appearance) = one manner/uniform

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一様|いちよう}に: uniformly, equally
- {一様|いちよう}な: uniform, alike
- {一様|いちよう}ではない: not uniform, varied

NOTE:
This word appears more often in written or formal contexts. In everyday speech, みんな{同|おな}じ (all the same) is more natural.
